Author: Pankaj Bhatia

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy./Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Nadeem Murtaza,Ankit Tripathi,Shashank Tilhari,Wali Nawaz Khan Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.0161 of 2024, under Section 105, 318(4) BNS,
P.S. Alapur, District Ambedkar Nagar.
3.

In terms of the FIR it was alleged that co-accused was running a hospital without having proper permits which was sealed on 18.06.2024 and a case was registered as Case Crime No.138 of 2024 Jeet Bahadur Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief ... on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96965245/
1 under Section 420 IPC & Section 15(2) of Indian Medical Council Act mainly on the allegation that the hospital was got registered on the address of some unknown person.

entities.text: Jeet Bahadur Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Subsequently, on 07.07.2024 information was received that the hospital was being run illegally.
It was also stated that a ward boy was seen to inspect the hospital, however, no one was found in the hospital; the seals were found to be intact.

Subsequently, certain medicines were seen which were related to delivery which were confiscated; on the basis of tyre marks, an apprehension was expressed that the hospital was being run illegally despite it being sealed.

It was also stated that on information it was revealed that one Ragini wife of Pintu was taken to the hospital for delivery and subsequently, she died during treatment and thus, it was stated that the accused who were running the hospital illegally were responsible for the death of the said person.
4.

My attention is also drawn to the statement of Pintu who had stated that his wife had died and funeral was also done, however, he was being pressurized to know as to why the postmortem was not got done.

The said application is on record as Annexure - 4.
5.
In the light of the said, the submission of counsel for the applicant is that despite there being no material, the applicant is being linked for an offence under Section 105, 318(4) of BNS.
6. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

7. Considering the facts including the statement of the husband of the deceased which is on record,
prima-facie, the material to implicate the applicant for the offence is not available, and apart from this, the applicant is around 70 years of age and has no criminal history apart from the present case and the case referred to in the FIR
, as such, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Jeet Bahadur Singh be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 14.8.2024 nishant  Jeet Bahadur Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief ... on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96965245/
